[NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) uses stacked causal dilated convolutions with residual connections. For reproducible parallel branches, specify every convolution’s kernel and dilation: each stride-1 convolution of width k and dilation d needs (k−1)d zeros on the left and no right padding. Branches d∈{1,2,4} must receive the same block input; combine their outputs with a per-position softmax gate and add the residual. Leakage-safe implementation recommendation: compute gates from h_t or a masked prefix summary through t, never whole-sequence pooling broadcast to earlier positions. Use channel-only LayerNorm at each position; temporal normalization can leak future information. Zero padding embeddings and reapply the nonpadding mask after intermediate transformations, especially before subsequent temporal convolutions, because biases and normalization offsets can create nonzero padding states. Position t predicts item t+1; left-padded inference reads the final nonpadding position.

Receptive-field accounting follows causal convolution composition, as in [WaveNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03499): sequential stride-1 convolutions have span R=1+Σ(k_l−1)d_l. Parallel branches take the maximum span, not the sum. Derived example: with k=3 and inherited span R_in, one convolution per branch gives spans R_in+2, R_in+4, R_in+8; two convolutions per branch at d and 2d give R_in+6d. These are bounding spans; exact accessible offsets can contain gaps. Therefore dilation-1 over deep features is not necessarily recent-context selection: its inputs already encode older history. Gates indicate preferences among transformations with overlapping inherited context. A prefix-summary gate can itself expand every gated output’s dependency to the whole prefix. Explicit recent-window semantics require branches built from raw embeddings or representations independently restricted to those windows. These implementation and interpretation points are deductions, not claims that NextItNet evaluated this gated variant.
